default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-428.title: Index-dollar decorrelation micro-break fade
E-428.hypothesis: WIN and WDO normally move against each other minute by minute because foreign flow trades both; when the rolling correlation of their 1-bar returns rises to near zero or positive, that macro flow is absent and each book is run by local liquidity providers, so a 15-minute box break in WIN has no persistent initiator behind it and is leaned back; fade it.

E-429.title: Absorbed break-bar fade
E-429.hypothesis: A close through the short box made by a bar that traded far more contracts per point of range than usual for its minute means the breakers met a large passive order that filled them without letting price run; the absorber holds the other side and the breakers are offside, so fade the break bar.

E-430.title: Wick-dominated tape micro-break fade
E-430.hypothesis: When recent bars close near where they opened while trading both ways inside the bar (small average body share of the range), every push inside a bar is answered within the same bar by resting liquidity; a 15-minute box break in such a two-way tape is one more intrabar-style probe that gets answered, so fade it.

E-431.title: Break toward the session VWAP follow
E-431.hypothesis: A short-box break that points toward a session VWAP lying several box heights away has room to run and a magnet ahead: benchmarked desks behind the VWAP are buyers (sellers) on the way back to value and the box's stops sit behind the break; follow only breaks in the direction of VWAP.

E-432.title: Break into today's heavy-volume zone fade
E-432.hypothesis: A short-box break whose next price bins already traded much more volume today than the session's average bin runs into the inventory of everyone who transacted there; those holders sell their break-even on the way up (buy it on the way down), so the break stalls in the heavy zone and reverts; fade it.

E-433.title: One-sided initial-balance extension break follow
E-433.hypothesis: When the session has extended beyond only one side of its initial balance, the other-timeframe participant has shown its hand in that direction and the opposite side has not even tested its edge; short-box breaks in the extension direction carry that initiator's continuing orders, so follow only those.

E-434.title: Multi-day streak break fade
E-434.hypothesis: After one or more consecutive down (up) daily closes, short-term holders are already loaded with the multi-day move and swing traders look for the bounce (short-horizon daily reversal); intraday breaks that extend the streak's direction are the last weak hands and get bought (sold), so fade only those breaks.

E-435.title: Prior-hour rejection-wick zone break fade
E-435.hypothesis: A completed clock hour with a long upper (lower) wick shows sellers (buyers) who rejected those prices an hour ago; a short-box break that carries the price back into that wick zone meets the same resting orders that made the wick, so fade the break while it is still inside the zone.

E-436.title: Neutral-momentum break fade
E-436.hypothesis: A short-box break that happens while the 14-bar RSI is still near 50 is a level giving way without any accumulated one-sided pressure behind it: the buyers and sellers of the last bars are balanced, so the break is a stop poke rather than a move, and the balanced book takes it back; fade it.

E-437.title: Even-volume tape micro-break fade
E-437.hypothesis: When bar volumes over the last window are much more even than usual (low coefficient of variation versus the previous sessions), trade is coming from steady market makers and time-sliced algos with no bursts of informed size; a 15-minute box break in that tape has no one-off initiator behind it, so fade it.
